title: VIABILITY: breeding reserve 90 -> 30 where food demonstrably pays?

identity.note: The probe always ran from the current checkout. A historical arm spec applied here is a settings replay, not a reproduction of its original figure.

preregistration.hypothesis: Step-3c analysis showed grazing income does not separate persisting from failing consumers (failures carry equal or greater graze energy; disease negligible; B/D<1 from the first checkpoints). The mapped gates point at the 90-tick breeding reserve against small consumer incomes. Rung 6 falsified rsur-30 in a different ecology (0.25 subsidy, uncoupled, unpaid graze); this tests the same dial where food demonstrably pays.
preregistration.prediction: cons > 0 on at least 12/18 AND prod > 0 on at least 12/18 seeds at tick 6000 (both machine criteria). Coexistence rate NOT predicted.
preregistration.falsification: FALSIFIED if cons = 0 on 7 or more of 18 seeds: the reserve is not the binding constraint — viability needs engine-level upkeep/damage economics, and that decision goes to the Owner with this record attached. No further reserve descent (30 -> 0 would breed from nothing and break the closed budget); no compensating light or subsidy moves.
preregistration.notPredicted: Coexistence rates, capture shares, extinction counts (descriptive), decomposer endpoints, per-win sizes.
confoundsControlled: Same 18-seed panel, horizon, engine, lifts, and 14/15 argvRest entries as graze-nutregen; the ONLY difference is positional rsur null -> 30 (argv slot 18)
Matched comparison against the archived nutregen run isolates the reserve effect
Null default (90) preserved in config; the arm exercises the sanctioned config path only
conservation enforced per seed at 0.5%; a seed above it fails the run rather than reporting

criteria.statement: consumers > 0 at tick 6000 on at least 12/18 seeds
producers > 0 at tick 6000 on at least 12/18 seeds
